Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.with, Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, Jdg.9:53, 2Ki.9:35); indecl. (exc. Mrk.15:22, -άν), 
 Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: Mat.27:33, Mrk.15:22, Jhn.19:17.†
 (AS)

δεῖπνον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for פַּת־בַּג (Da) ;] 
the chief meal of the day, dinner, supper: Mat.23:6, Mrk.12:39, Luk.14:17, 24 20:46, Jhn.13:2, 4 21:20, 1Co.11:21; δ. ποιεῖν, Mrk.6:21, Luk.14:12, 16, Jhn.12:2; κυριακὸν (which see) δ., 1Co.11:20; metaphorically (Dalman, Words, 118), δ. τ. γάμου τ. ἀρνίου, Rev.19:9; δ. τ. μέγα τ. Θεοῦ, Rev.19:17.†
 (AS)

lightness: levity , (New Testament) 
from ἐλαφρός (ML)

ἐπι-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (ἐπιατέλλω), [in LXX for אִגֶּרֶת, etc.; frequently in Mac ;] 
__1. a message. 
 __2. a letter, an epistle: Act.9:2, 1Co.5:9, al.; pl., Act.22:5, 1Co.16:3, al.; ἐ. σνστατικαί, 2Co.3:1 (cf. Milligan, NTD, 254 f.). (On the NT ἐπιστολαί, cf. Milligan, Th., 121 ff.; NTD, 85 ff.; Deiss., BS, 3 ff.; St. Paul, 8 ff.)
 (AS)

1. courage, boldness , (Homer), attic; θ. τινός courage to do a thing, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. that which gives courage , θάρση grounds of confidence , (Euripides) 
3. in bad sense, audacity , (Iliad by Homer): compare θράσος. (ML)

θρῆσκος
 (-κός, WH), -ον, ό 
religious, careful of the outward forms of divine service (see previous word)): Jas.1:26.†
 SYN.: εὐσεβής, θεοσεβής, δεισιδαίμων (see Tr., Syn., § xlviii) (AS)

Ἱεροσολυμεῖτης (WH, Ἰερ-; Rec. -μίτης), -ου, ὁ, 
 [in LXX: Sir.50:27 (28) 2Ma.4:22 2Mac 4:39 (V* -μήτης) 2Ma 18:5* ;] 
an inhabitant of Jerusalem: Mrk.1:5, Jhn.7:25.†
 (AS)

κάκωσις, -εως, ἡ
 (κακόω) [Ín LXX (for עָנִי, יָדַע, etc.): Exo.3:7, Jer.2:28, Wis.3:2, al. ;] 
ill-treatment: Act.7:34 (LXX),†
 (AS)

ἀ-μέμπτως, 
 adv. (ἄμεμπτος), [in LXX: Est.3:13 * ;] 
blamelessly (Lft., Notes, 28, 89; MM, VGT, see word -ος): 1Th.2:10 3:13 WH mg., 5:23.†
 (AS)

κιθαρίζω 
 [in LXX: Isa.23:16 (נָגַן pi.)* ;] 
to play upon the lyre or harp: 1Co.14:7, Rev.14:2.†
 (AS)

κλίβανος, -ον, ό
 (Att.., κρίβ-, but κλ- in Ion., Hdt., ii, 92), [in LXX for תַּנּוּר, Gen.15:17, Hos.7:4, 6 al. ;] 
__1. in cl., a clibanus, cribanus, an earthen vessel for baking bread. 
 __2. In LXX and NT, a furnace (cf. MM, Exp., xv), an oven: Mat.6:30, Luk.12:28.†
 (AS)

κτάομαι, -ῶμαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָנָה ;] 
in pres., impf., fut. and aor., to procure for oneself, get, gain, acquire (the pf. and plpf., to have acquired, hence to possess, do not occur in NT): with accusative of thing(s), Mat.10:9, Luk.18:12, Act.8:20; with genitive pret., Act.22:28; ἐκ with genitive pret., Act.1:18; τ,ψυχὰς ὑμῶν (MM, xvi), Luk.21:19; τ. ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι, 1Th.4:4 (where if σ. = body, κ. must = pf., κέκτημαι; see MM, xvi; M, Th., in l; Field, Notes, 72 f. But σ. is most frequently taken as = wife; see Thayer, see word; Lft., Notes, 53 ff.; ICC, in l).†
 (AS)

Μάρκος, -ου, ὁ, 
 Mark: Mk., title., Act.12:12, 25 15:37, 39, Col.4:10, 2Ti.4:11, Phm 24, 1Pe.5:13 (see Swete, Mk., Intr., xiii ff.; DB, iii, 245 ff).†
 (AS)

παρα-καλύπτω 
 [in LXX: Isa.44:8 (פָּחַד), Eze.22:26 (עָלַם hi.)* ;] 
to cover by hanging something beside, to hide: metaphorically (as Plat., al.), Luk.9:45.†
 (AS)

περπερεύοραι
 (περπερος, vainglorious) 
to boast or vaunt oneself: 1Co.13:4 (elsewhere. only in Antonin.; see Abbott, Essays, 87).†
 (AS)

προσ-εργάζομαι 
 __1. to work or do service besides (Hdt., Plut.). 
 __2. to gain besides, by working or trading: Luk.19:16 (Xen.).†
 (AS)

προσ-κεφάλαιον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX: Eze.13:18, 20 (כֶּסֶת), I Est.3:8 * ;] 
a pillow, cushion: Mrk.4:38.†
 (AS)

συν-χράομαι
 (Rec. συγ-), -ῶμαι, [in Al.: 1Ki.30:19 * ;] 
to use together with. Metaphorical, with dative of person(s), to associate with: Jhn.4:9 (Polyb., a1.).†
 (AS)

ταπείνωσις, -εως, ἡ
 (ταπεινόω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי ;] 
abasement, humiliation, low estate: Luk.1:48, Act.8:33" (LXX), Php.3:21, Jas.1:10 (Plat., Arist., and later writers).†
 (AS)

ὑγρός, -ά, -όν, 
 [in LXX: Jdg.16:7,8 (לַח), Job.8:16 (רָשׂב), Sir.39:13 
wet, moist, opposite to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green: Luk.23:31.†
 (AS)

φίλητός (T, Φιλητός), -ου, ὁ 
 Philetus: 2Ti.2:17.†
 (AS)

φιμόω, -ῶ
 (φιμός, a muzzle), [in LXX: Deu.25:4 (חָסַם), Dan LXX Su 1:61, 4Ma.1:35 א R * ;] 
to muzzle: 1Co.9:9, 1Ti.5:18" (LXX) ; metaphorically, to put to silence: with accusative of person(s), Mat.22:34, 1Pe.2:15; pass., to be silenced, silent: Mat.22:12, Mrk.1:25 4:39, Luk.4:35.†
 (AS)

χόρτασμα, -τος, τό
 (χορτάζω), [in LXX: Gen.24:25, 32 42:27 43:24, Jdg.19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), Deu.11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Sir.33:24) Sir.38:26 * ;] 
fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Act.7:11 (RV, sustenance).†
 (AS)

A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.13; 
 son of: Reuel (H7467); 
 brother of: Nahath (H5184), Shammah (H8048) and Mizzah (H4199)
 § Zerah or Zarah = "rising"
1) a son of Reuel and grandson of Esau, one of the dukes of the Edomites
2) twin brother of Pharez, sons of Judah and Tamar; descendants are called Zarhites, Ezrahites, and Izrahites
3) son of Simeon; also called 'Zohar'
4) a Gershonite Levite, son of Iddo of Adaiah
5) the Ethiopian or Cushite, invader of Judah in the reign of Asa who defeated the invaders; probably the same as the Egyptian king Usarken I, second king of the Egyptian 22nd dynasty or perhaps more probably Usarken II, his 2nd successor
6) another Edomite leader; possibly same as 1
